from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            Create(cycle_path),

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Intuition: The Harmonic Symphony", [
            "Any complex wave is a sum of simple harmonics.",
            "Think of this like stacking musical notes.",
            "Sine waves combine into a square wave.",
            "Frequencies and amplitudes define our unique waveform.",
            "The harmonic symphony reveals hidden structures."
        ])

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Construction", [
            "The Fourier series constructs complex periodic signals.",
            "Each term acts as a weighted harmonic.",
            "a₀ represents the signal's average height.",
            "aₙ and bₙ are volume knobs for frequencies.",
            "Adjusting coefficients reshapes the final function."
        ])
        
        # Formula elements
        formula = MathTex(
            "f(x) = \\frac{a_0}{2} + \\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty} (a_n \\cos(nx) + b_n \\sin(nx))"
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight coefficients
        an = formula.get_parts_by_tex("a_n")
        bn = formula.get_parts_by_tex("b_n")
        weights = VGroup(an, bn)
        self.play(weights.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        a0 = formula.get_parts_by_tex("a_0")
        self.play(a0.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Re-highlight coefficients as knobs
        self.play(weights.animate.set_color("#FF8800"))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF8800"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Final color shift to show full interaction
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We extract coefficients using the principle of orthogonality.",
            "Signal passes through specific frequency gates.",
            "The integral acts as a mathematical prism."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Calculation via Orthogonality", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        vec_s = Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        vec_c = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP, color=WHITE)
        vgroup_ortho = VGroup(vec_s, vec_c)
        
        prism_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/prism.svg")
        filter_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/filter.svg")
        
        inner_prod_text = MathTex(r"\langle s, c \rangle = 0", color=RED)
        
        signal = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(2 * np.pi * x) + 0.5 * np.cos(4 * np.pi * x), x_range=[-1, 1], color=TEAL)
        projection = Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.5, color=TEAL)
        
        c_n_label = MathTex(r"c_n", color=YELLOW)
        
        integral_simpl = MathTex(r"\int f(x) e^{-inx} dx = c_n", color=GREEN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(vgroup_ortho, "A1", "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(prism_img, "B2", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(vec_s), Create(vec_c), FadeIn(prism_img))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(inner_prod_text, "D2")
        self.play(Write(inner_prod_text))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(signal, "A3", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(projection, "D4")
        self.play(Create(signal), Create(projection))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(c_n_label, "E4")
        self.play(Write(c_n_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(integral_simpl, "E2", "F5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(filter_img, "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(integral_simpl), FadeIn(filter_img))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application & Summary", [
            "Fourier series allow efficient signal processing.",
            "Removing frequencies shrinks file sizes.",
            "We decompose signals to understand and reconstruct."
        ])
        
        # Audio Signal Visual
        audio_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * PI * t) + 0.2 * np.sin(7 * PI * t), x_range=[-2, 2])
        self.place_in_area(audio_wave, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Frequency Spectrum
        freq_bars = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=1 + i*0.5, width=0.3, fill_opacity=1) for i in range(5)])
        freq_bars.arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(freq_bars, 'D2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(audio_wave), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(freq_bars), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        summary_text = Text("Decomposition = Understanding & Compression", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(summary_text, 'F3')
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Periodic Motion
sections.content: Briefly define a periodic function f(x) = f(x + T). Use a visual of a pendulum swinging back and forth. Emphasize that all complex periodic phenomena can be seen as a 'sum' of simpler, harmonious movements.
sections.example: The rhythmic heartbeat of a blue whale, represented as a repeating wave pattern on a monitor.

sections.title: The Core Intuition: The Harmonic Symphony
sections.content: Introduce the idea that any complex wave (a square, saw, or heart pulse) is just a collection of pure sine and cosine waves with different frequencies and amplitudes. Visual: An animation showing three simple sine waves stacking up to transform into a square wave.
sections.example: A musical chord: Hearing one rich sound that is actually a combination of several pure, individual notes played simultaneously.

sections.title: The Mathematical Construction
sections.content: Present the Fourier Series formula: f(x) = a₀/2 + Σ(aₙ cos(nx) + bₙ sin(nx)). Explain the roles: 'a₀' is the DC offset (average height), and 'aₙ, bₙ' are the 'weights' or 'volume knobs' for each frequency.
sections.example: A DJ mixing console: Each slider (coefficient) controls how much of a specific frequency (sine wave) is added to the final mix.

sections.title: Calculation via Orthogonality
sections.content: Explain that we extract coefficients by taking the 'projection' (integral) of the target function against sine and cosine bases. Visual: A 'filter' animation where a signal passes through different frequency gates.
sections.example: Using a prism to split white light into its constituent rainbow colors; the math acts as the prism for the signal.

sections.title: Real-World Application & Summary
sections.content: Conclude by showing how Fourier Series enable modern technology. Recap: We broke a complex wave into simple parts to understand, process, and reconstruct it.
sections.example: MP3 compression: Removing 'inaudible' higher-frequency components (Fourier coefficients) to shrink the file size while keeping the song recognizable.
